verdict.rationale: New Relic does publish some pricing info (100GB free ingest tier) on its pricing page, giving a baseline for self-service cost estimation without sales contact, but multiple independent community reports describe billing as opaque and unpredictable in practice—per-user pricing changes causing 20x bill increases, environments/redundant AZs billed as extra 'production' instances, and ingest spikes (e.g. JFR enabled by default) sextupling costs unexpectedly. This directly contradicts the 'predict costs transparently' premise even though a published price list exists. Missing for 10: detailed per-signal (e.g., per-host, per-user, per-GB-by-data-type) pricing breakdown, and evidence that published prices reliably predict actual bills without support intervention.
